ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The principal AML/CFT statute is the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, together with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Requirements and Compliance) Regulations 2011 and applicable AML/CFT supervisor guidance. The Companies Act 1993 governs company registration and shareholding disclosures. New Zealand does not maintain a general, publicly searchable central register of beneficial owners of ordinary companies equivalent to a statutory UBO register. Companies must maintain statutory registers and provide prescribed information to the Registrar of Companies. AML/CFT reporting entities must conduct customer due diligence, including identifying and taking reasonable steps to verify beneficial owners and persons exercising effective control, under the AML/CFT Act.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relevant company registry or other competent public authority in the document's country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: New Zealand AML/CFT reporting entities must apply customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence where legally required, including for politically exposed persons and higher-risk situations, under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and related regulations. Screen relevant customers, beneficial owners, controllers, and counterparties against applicable United Nations Security Council sanctions and New Zealand domestic sanctions measures. OFAC screening is not a general New Zealand statutory requirement, but may be required by US nexus, correspondent banking, contractual, or risk policies. Retain risk-based screening and escalation records.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online services, operated by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name must be reserved before incorporation under the Companies Act 1993. The proposed name must satisfy statutory restrictions and must not be identical or almost identical to a name already reserved or registered, or otherwise be prohibited or misleading. A name may use English or other permitted characters supported by the Companies Office system. There is no general requirement that an ordinary company name be supplied in Maori or another local-language script.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words suggesting a connection with the Crown, government, local authority, or public authority where that connection is not authorized
Words or expressions restricted by statute or requiring the consent of a specified authority
Names that are identical or almost identical to an existing registered or reserved company name
Names that are offensive, misleading, or otherwise prohibited by law
Words suggesting a regulated professional, financial, charitable, or other protected status where use is restricted or consent is required
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is generally valid for 20 working days. If rejected, review the Companies Office notice and the Companies Act 1993 grounds, correct the proposed name, and submit a fresh reservation application. Where the applicant disputes a Registrar decision, request reconsideration or use the applicable statutory review or appeal route, observing the decision notice and statutory deadlines; an appeal from a Registrar decision may be available to the District Court under the Companies Act 1993. A reservation is not incorporation and does not determine trademark rights. Conduct separate searches of the Companies Register and Intellectual Property Office of New Zealand trade mark records.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A New Zealand company must have a registered office and an address for service in New Zealand. A commercial provider's address may be used if it is a genuine address at which statutory notices and records can be received and the company can meet its record-keeping and access obligations. A mailbox-only address is not an adequate substitute. A translation and dubbing agency has no industry-specific registered-office or local-substance requirement merely by reason of its stated business activity. Banks, payment providers, tax authorities, and AML/CFT reporting entities may separately require evidence of actual operations, management, or customer activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No authoritative public statistic quantifies the probability of an unannounced physical inspection for this activity. No routine industry-specific inspection requirement has been identified for an unlicensed translation and media-dubbing agency; inspection or information requests may nevertheless occur under applicable company, tax, employment, consumer, privacy, or AML/CFT enforcement powers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 10-14 (registration and certificate of incorporation), 15-16 (constitution and registered office), 20-22 (company names), 36-38 (share capital), 44-45 (allotment of shares), 48 (no-par-value shares), 84 (share register), 88 (director register), 89 (director interests), 102 (register of charges), 124 (share certificates), 149-153 (director appointment), 180 (board resolutions), 200 (address for service); Companies (Registration) Regulations 1993; New Zealand Business Number Act 2016; Financial Reporting Act 2013.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the Companies Register (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz); co-ordinates with the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZCN - Application for Registration of a Company (lodged electronically via the Companies Register online portal, accompanied by signed consents to act of each director and shareholder).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under the Companies Act 1993 a company limited by shares may be incorporated with one or more shares of no par value, fully paid or partly paid, with no statutory minimum issued capital, no authorised capital requirement and no escrow or fund-locking condition. The International Company requires at least one shareholder and one share; non-resident ownership is unrestricted, and no capital deposit is required at incorporation or at any time thereafter.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] (the 'Company') - passed by unanimous written resolution of the sole/collective director(s) pursuant to section 180 of the Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand) on this [___] day of [__________], 20[__]:

1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: The subscribers and share allotments recorded in the Application for Registration (Form NZCN) are hereby ratified; the board approves the subscription of [number] ordinary shares by each subscribing shareholder as set out in the Register of Shareholders, and directs that such shares be allotted and issued fully paid, without par value, and without any requirement for escrow or deposit of capital.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE AND ADDRESS FOR SERVICE: The registered office of the Company shall be and is hereby fixed at [Street Number, Street, Suburb, City, Postcode], New Zealand, being a physical address in New Zealand for service of documents; the address for service shall be as notified to the Companies Register. The directors are authorised to notify the Registrar of Companies of the registered office and address for service in accordance with sections 16 and 200 of the Companies Act 1993, and to change such addresses from time to time as the board determines.

3. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: [Name of New Zealand-resident director] is hereby appointed as sole director (or as one of the directors) of the Company pursuant to sections 151 and 153 of the Companies Act 1993; [Name] is hereby appointed as Chief Executive Officer; [Name] is hereby appointed as Chief Financial Officer; [Name] is hereby appointed as Company Secretary. Each officer shall serve until removal by the board and shall exercise the powers delegated by this board, subject to the constitution of the Company (if any) and the Companies Act 1993.

4. BANKING AND PAYMENT RAILS: The directors are hereby authorised to open corporate bank accounts with such banks as they select and to establish the Wise B2B and Payoneer payment rails for international client invoicing and vendor payments; the authorised signatory list attached to this resolution is adopted and the opening of such accounts is ratified.

5. INCIDENTAL AND DELEGATED ACTIONS: Each officer is hereby authorised, jointly and severally, to execute and file all documents and to do all acts necessary to give full effect to these resolutions, including the filing of Form NZCN, IRD tax registrations, GST and ACC registrations, NZBN verification, lease execution, engagement of accountants and legal counsel, and any other step required for the statutory incorporation and operational commencement of the Company. This resolution is effective immediately and remains in full force until revoked by the board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search, Approval and Director/Shareholder Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - online Companies Register portal (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz), under the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search on the Companies Register to confirm the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and does not contravene sections 21-22 of the Companies Act 1993. Where the name is available, either reserve it online (optional, fee NZ$10.60 inclusive of GST, approximately US$6.50) or proceed directly to incorporation using the standard name-approval pathway embedded in Form NZCN. Simultaneously obtain from each proposed director and each proposed shareholder a personally signed and dated consent to act in such capacity; verify that at least one director will be ordinarily resident in New Zealand (section 151 Companies Act 1993), with the Australian-resident director exemption available only where the company qualifies as a large company or maintains a New Zealand agent. If the company is to adopt a constitution, instruct a New Zealand solicitor to finalise the draft at this stage.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (with up to three alternative names)
Consent to act as director (Form NZCN Part A) signed by each director
Consent to act as shareholder (Form NZCN Part B) signed by each shareholder
Residential address, date of birth and occupation of each director
Physical registered office address in New Zealand (street address, not a PO Box)
New Zealand address for service (physical or electronic)
Draft constitution (optional, if the company wishes to depart from the default rules of the Companies Act 1993)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses the proposed name as unacceptable or confusingly similar (ss 21-22), the applicant may: (i) submit a written submission requesting the Registrar exercise discretion to approve the name on the ground of distinctiveness or prior goodwill; (ii) elect the next available alternate name and re-file; or (iii) after refusal, apply for judicial review in the High Court. Name refusals do not otherwise invalidate the incorporation application where an alternate name is substituted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Application for Registration (Form NZCN) and Payment of the Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - electronic Companies Register filing platform (web-based lodgement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the online Form NZCN - Application for Registration of a Company. Populate the company name, physical registered office address (must be a New Zealand street address), address for service, director details (including consents), shareholder details, share capital structure (default: no-par-value ordinary shares), and attach the constitution if one has been adopted. Each person named as a director or shareholder must sign the application or consent form in accordance with section 10(2) of the Companies Act 1993. Confirm the corporate shareholder is duly authorised (attach a board resolution of the corporate shareholder where relevant). Pay the incorporation fee of NZ$105.30 (approximately US$64) by electronic payment. Submit; the Registrar will process the application and, upon satisfaction of all statutory conditions, register the company under section 12.
required_dossiers: Completed Form NZCN with all statutory particulars
Signed consent to act of each director
Signed consent to act of each shareholder
Company constitution (if any, otherwise the Companies Act 1993 default rules apply)
Board resolution of any corporate shareholder authorising the subscription
Evidence of the physical registered office address (e.g., lease, land title record, or agent's acknowledgment)
Payment of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Under section 12(3) of the Companies Act 1993, the Registrar may make a requisition requiring further information or correction of the application; the applicant has 20 working days from service of the requisition to respond, failing which the application is deemed withdrawn and any fee is refunded. If the Registrar declines to register, the applicant may resubmit a corrected application without prejudice, and any final refusal may be challenged by judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand (Judicature Amendment Act 1972 procedure).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation, Company Number and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Certificate of Incorporation and Company Number) and MBIE NZBN Team (allocation of the New Zealand Business Number)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Registrar files the Certificate of Incorporation in the Companies Register and issues a certified copy to the company, certifying the company name, registration number, date of incorporation and that the liability of members is limited (section 14 Companies Act 1993). The Certificate together with the company extract constitutes prima facie evidence of incorporation. Simultaneously, MBIE issues the company a unique 13-digit New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) under the New Zealand Business Number Act 2016, which interoperates with all government agency services. The directors should download the Certificate of Incorporation, the company extract, and the NZBN confirmation from the Companies Register, and verify the correctness of all registered particulars.
required_dossiers: No further filing required upon registration
Resultant official documents: Certificate of Incorporation
Companies Register company extract (public record snapshot)
NZBN confirmation notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation or company extract contains any error, the company should file a 'change of particulars' notification with the Companies Office or apply to the Registrar for rectification under section 360 of the Companies Act 1993. Lost or damaged certificates can be replaced by requesting a certified copy electronically (fee approximately NZ$2.50 per page). Disputes as to the date or validity of incorporation are resolved by production of the Register entry, which is conclusive absent fraud.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations with Inland Revenue (IRD Number, GST, PAYE) and ACC Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) - online services via RealMe or Form IR596; Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) for the employer Work Account levy
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the company's IRD number online through the IRD business registration portal, or by filing Form IR596 with the IRD within three months of incorporation. Register for Goods and Services Tax (GST) immediately if annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed NZ$60,000 (compulsory registration); voluntary registration is available for lower-turnover businesses and is advisable for B2B localization services to claim input credits. If the company will employ editors, voice artists, project managers or other staff, register as an employer for PAYE and KiwiSaver, and enrol for the ACC Work Account (a statutory levy imposed on all employers for workplace injury cover). Enrolment in the PEPPOL e-invoicing network is recommended for the electronic issuance of GST-compliant invoices to government and corporate clients. For cross-border receipts, the company may use the Wise B2B or Payoneer payment rails; these rails are not tax registrations and do not displace the IRD reporting obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN confirmation
Registered office and service address details
Director personal details and IRD numbers of directors (if resident)
Description of business activity (ISIC 7490 - professional translation and media localization)
Anticipated annual turnover and GST filing frequency election
Bank account details for IRD refunds
Employer details and intended first PAYE payday (if hiring staff)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD queries the application (for example, requesting proof of the business address), the company should respond with a copy of the registered-office lease, a utility bill, or a statutory declaration from the registered agent. If the IRD number is not issued within the service standard, escalate through the IRD contact centre or instruct a tax agent. Late-registration penalties may be remitted by IRD under the discretionary powers in section 183 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 upon written application setting out reasonable cause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Statutory Registers, Corporate Records and Corporate Bank Account with Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's registered office (statutory books); New Zealand-registered banks and licensed payment service providers for corporate banking and the Wise B2B / Payoneer rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The board must cause the company to prepare and thereafter maintain at its registered office the statutory registers mandated by the Companies Act 1993: the share register (s 84), register of directors (s 88), register of directors' interests in shares (s 89), and register of charges (s 102), together with minute books of board and shareholder meetings and a copy of the constitution (if any). Resolve to open a corporate current account with a New Zealand bank or a licensed non-bank financial institution, and authorise the onboarding of the Wise B2B and Payoneer rails for international settlement. Execute the bank mandate forms and provide the institution with standard AML/CFT customer due diligence documentation under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; for a translation/localization agency the banking AML/CFT risk tier is Low-Risk Standard, requiring ordinary identity, address and source-of-funds verification.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Companies Register extract (not older than three months)
Board resolution resolving to open the account and authorising signatories
Passport or government-issued identity document of each authorised signatory
Ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) declarations for holders of 25% or more of the shares
NZBN and IRD confirmation of registration
Brief business plan and projected revenue for ISIC 7490 services
Client agreement or sample invoices evidencing the localization trade
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the financial institution issues a query on the CDD/AML package, the company supplies supplementary evidence such as the lease, the registered office agent's letter, or a Notarised Certificate of Incumbency. If the bank declines to open the account, the company may lodge a complaint with the New Zealand Banking Ombudsman Scheme, or make a new application with another registered bank or licensed non-bank provider; there is no statutory right of acceptance in New Zealand, but the low-risk nature of the translation business should normally facilitate approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Workplace Compliance: Health and Safety, Fire Safety, Building Warrant of Fitness and Studio Acoustic Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: WorkSafe New Zealand (occupational health and safety); Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ); territorial authority (Building Act 2004 warrant of fitness regime); Accreditated Independent Qualified Persons (IQP) for compliance schedules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: As a Person Conducting a Business or Undertaking (PCBU), the company must comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015: draft and implement a health and safety policy, a hazard register, and an emergency plan proportionate to an office-based professional services activity. Verify that the leased premises hold a current Building Warrant of Fitness (BWoF) covering all safety systems (fire alarms, emergency lighting, sprinklers) as required by sections 108-112 of the Building Act 2004; obtain the annual compliance schedule from the landlord or the body corporate. For a media dubbing operation, confirm that the use of sound studio booths is permitted under the local district plan (resource consent for noise where required) and conduct an acoustic verification against AS/NZS 2107:2016. All electrical equipment used for editing and dubbing must be tested and tagged to AS/NZS 3760. Register with ACC for the employer levy and complete the WorkSafe self-assessment for the business.
required_dossiers: Current Building Warrant of Fitness and compliance schedule (obtained from the landlord)
Fire evacuation plan and FENZ acknowledgment (where more than 100 persons occupy the workplace)
Health and safety policy, hazard register and emergency procedures
AS/NZS 3760 electrical test and tag records for sound/editing equipment
Acoustic insulation assessment report for dubbing studios (against AS/NZS 2107:2016)
District plan noise compliance statement or resource consent for studio use (if applicable)
ACC Work Account registration acknowledgement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If WorkSafe or the territorial authority identifies a non-compliance, a compliance or improvement notice is issued under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015; the company must remedy the defect within the stated period (typically two to four weeks, extendable on application). Where the premises lack a Building Warrant of Fitness, the landlord must commission the necessary inspections through an Independent Qualified Person; if the landlord fails to act, the tenant may commission the IQP itself and recover costs, and in serious cases the territorial authority may issue a dangerous building notice demanding rectification or closure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industry-specific licensing board regulates ISIC 7490 (professional multilingual translation and media dubbing) in New Zealand. General commerce oversight is exercised by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) through the Companies Office and by the Commerce Commission under the Fair Trading Act 1986, the Consumer Guarantees Act 1993 and the Privacy Act 2020; the Commerce Commission regulates business-to-consumer conduct but does not issue an operating licence.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating permit or manufacturing licence is required for the provision of translation, localization, subtitling or media dubbing services in New Zealand. Voluntary quality certifications (ISO 17100 for translation services and ISO 9001 for quality management) may be adopted for commercial assurance but are not mandated by law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) of New Zealand, administering the Resource Management Act 1991 and national environmental standards in co-ordination with regional councils and territorial authorities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category: No EIA Required. Schedule 4 of the Resource Management Act 1991 and the national free-company identification framework do not list office-based professional services or media production/localization as an activity requiring a full Environmental Impact Assessment, an EPA national interest determination, or a registration under section 111 of the RMA. A dubbing studio that emits no industrial discharges is treated as a standard commercial office activity under the local district plan.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source industrial wastewater, VOC or air emissions arise from a translation/localization office. Compliance thresholds that do apply: (i) office sanitary effluent must discharge to the territorial authority's municipal sewers under the local trade-waste bylaw, with no contaminant levels exceeding permitted domestic wastewater parameters; (ii) any sound studio must meet district plan noise limits, typically 40-50 dB LAeq during night hours, assessed under AS/NZS 2107:2016 for acoustic insulation; (iii) HVAC and ventilation discharges must comply with the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (NES-AQ) for any contaminant emissions, including PM10 and odour thresholds; (iv) electronic waste (computers, recording hardware, media storage) must be tracked and disposed of under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008, with priority given to the national e-waste recycling schemes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: compliance with NZ Building Code clauses C1-C6 and FENZ fire evacuation scheme approval for workplaces with more than 100 persons; a valid Building Warrant of Fitness with annual compliance schedule (Building Act 2004 ss 108-112) is mandatory. Structural clearance: the tenant fit-out must not compromise fire cells or structural ratings, and any renovation works that alter the building's fire safety or structure require a building consent from the territorial authority. Occupational clearance: registration with WorkSafe New Zealand as a PCBU and with ACC for the mandatory employer levy; compliance with workplace exposure standards (WES) for indoor air quality and noise under the Health and Safety at Work (General Risk and Workplace Management) Regulations 2016; electrical safety testing to AS/NZS 3760 for all studio and editing equipment; notifiable incident reporting under the HSWA 2015 to WorkSafe within 48 hours.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: the premises must operate under a current Building Warrant of Fitness with a compliance schedule covering fire alarms, emergency lighting, and fire suppression, together with a FENZ fire evacuation scheme where applicable. Structural: all occupancy loads and fit-outs must be within the building's structural rating, with any alteration to firecells requiring a building consent from the territorial authority. Occupational: the company must register with WorkSafe New Zealand as a PCBU, register with ACC for the mandatory employer levy, implement a written health and safety policy with hazard and incident registers, perform periodic electrical testing (AS/NZS 3760), and conduct acoustic monitoring of dubbing booths to AS/NZS 2107:2016 to protect worker hearing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake), Government of New Zealand; digital portal: myIR (https://www.myir.ird.govt.nz), supplemented by the New Zealand Companies Office (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz) for corporate registration and NZBN issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity (e.g., a Cook Islands International Company) carrying on business in New Zealand must: (1) register as an overseas company with the New Zealand Companies Office on the Companies Register and obtain a New Zealand Company Number and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN); (2) apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number using form IR596 (non-resident company carrying on a taxable activity in NZ) or IR742 (non-resident company deriving New Zealand-sourced income without a taxable activity); (3) provide certified certificate of incorporation, constitution, directors' and shareholders' details, the registered office or New Zealand agent for service of process, and the date of commencement of New Zealand business; (4) register for GST on the same application or subsequently via myIR, specifying the expected turnover to trigger the appropriate filing frequency (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly); and (5) in parallel, register as an employer with IRD (IR334/IR335 forms) if the New Zealand operation will employ staff in-country.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a check-the-box classification regime. Available elections applicable to a foreign International Company include: (i) GST group registration election under sections 55-58 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 to consolidate the New Zealand branch with other group companies; (ii) election to file GST on a payments basis under section 19G of the GST Act 1985 where taxable supplies do not exceed NZD 2,000,000 in a 12-month period; (iii) election to zero-rate cross-border services on a B2B basis with written confirmation from the non-resident recipient; and (iv) application of the hybrid and branch mismatch neutralisation rules in Part FM and sections FH 1-FH 11 of the Income Tax Act 2007, which require the entity and its New Zealand permanent establishment to document any hybrid financial instrument or branch payment arrangements and align tax outcomes to avoid double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a destination-based value-added tax under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies (including remote/digital services such as multilingual translation and media dubbing) made in New Zealand or supplied to New Zealand resident non-GST-registered consumers in any rolling 12-month period, which triggers mandatory registration; voluntary registration is permitted where a taxable activity is carried on, and cross-border B2B supplies to GST-registered New Zealand recipients are reverse-charged and excluded from the registration threshold for non-resident suppliers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or transaction-level government clearance regime exists in New Zealand. Electronic invoicing is voluntary and operates through the Peppol network (Te Papa Whakatu) supporting PEPPOL BIS 3.0. Inland Revenue requires all registered taxpayers to file GST returns (GST101) electronically through myIR, which is the statutory digital filing channel, but no API-based pre-approval of invoices is mandated. Tax invoices must be issued within 28 days of the time of supply, and all GST records must be retained for seven years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the GST Act 1985 for: (i) supplies of goods physically exported by the supplier within 28 days of the time of supply (section 11(1)(a)-(ab)); (ii) services supplied to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, provided the services are not supplied to a New Zealand-resident private consumer and are not directly in connection with land situated in New Zealand or goods in New Zealand at the time of supply (section 11(1)(c)-(d)); (iii) services supplied to a non-resident person for the benefit of goods that are in New Zealand at the time of supply but are subsequently exported (section 11(1)(e)); (iv) remote services supplied by a non-resident supplier to a New Zealand GST-registered business (B2B zero-rating); and (v) translation, localization, and media dubbing services delivered entirely offshore to foreign clients, where the supplier holds a valid certificate of non-residence signed by the overseas customer (the 'as far as we know' certificate under section 11(3)) and the services are performed or enjoyed outside New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EXD) lodged through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window (for physically exported goods such as master media or dubbing assets)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign exchange (FX) settlement advice from a New Zealand bank or a Wise B2B / Payoneer payout record evidencing receipt of consideration from the overseas buyer
Signed certificate of non-residence of the overseas customer (IRD-approved 'as far as we know' certificate)
Original GST tax invoice and the underlying contract or purchase order identifying the non-resident recipient and the services performed
Proof of offshore performance and delivery (production files, dubbing studio logs, or digital delivery confirmation to the foreign client)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue actively audits zero-rating claims and may re-characterise a supply as standard-rated where statutory conditions are not met, causing the GST to be clawed back together with penalties and use-of-money interest. If exported goods are not exported within 28 days or are diverted to the New Zealand market, the supply is standard-rated in the period of divergence. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 are: 20% for lack of reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, 150% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion; fraudulent zero-rating, forged export documentation, or deliberately falsified FX repatriation records also attract criminal liability under sections 143A-144 of the Tax Administration Act 1994, with maximum fines of NZD 50,000 for individuals and NZD 250,000 for companies, liability for reputational disqualification, imprisonment of up to 5 years in serious evasion cases, and extension of the standard 4-year assessment period where fraud is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua); statutory oversight of the New Zealand Foreign Exchange Act 2010, the AML/CFT Act 2009, and the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989, with the Financial Markets Authority and the Department of Internal Affairs supervising non-bank financial institutions
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully convertible on both current and capital account. New Zealand maintains no exchange controls, no foreign-exchange approval gates, and no limitations on the repatriation of dividends, loan repayments, or liquidation proceeds. Profit remittance is subject only to standard tax obligations, including Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) at domestic or applicable double-tax-agreement rates, and the bank's ordinary documentary verification. Capital inflows and outflows can be freely routed through any Registered Bank, provided transactions meet the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's statistical reporting thresholds for balance-of-payments purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no mandatory export-proceeds surrender, no minimum conversion ratio, and no statutory timeline for repatriation of export receipts. The International Company may retain 100% of foreign-currency earnings in domestic or offshore foreign-currency accounts for an unlimited period and may convert to NZD at market rates at its sole discretion. Reporting applies only for statistical balance-of-payments purposes through the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's international transactions reporting system, not for exchange-control purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (NZD Current and Foreign Currency Multi-Currency)
Operational Account and Trade Finance Facility
Operational Account (NZD with FX Forward Capability)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Wise is rated High for international collections and disbursements because it is a New Zealand-founded, FMC-registered, globally licensed EMI with compliant NZ AML/CFT registration and local settlement rails in NZD, USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, and 30+ corridors. Payoneer is rated Medium: it is fully viable for outbound disbursements to localization contractors and media vendors and for inbound collections from global marketplaces, but it cannot substitute for a Registered Bank because it cannot provide credit, commercial letters of credit, or formal FX hedging. Offshore EMIs not registered under the NZ AML/CFT Act 2009 face a legal constraint: they cannot maintain solicited relationships with New Zealand counterparties and must not handle core treasury settlement flows of an International Company without a locally registered agent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence in New Zealand is not an absolute statutory mandate for low-risk, NZ-resident clients. For an International Company with non-resident ownership and a Tax-Exempt-Zone classification, the mandatory baseline is enhanced due diligence: each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner at the 25% threshold must complete verified identity documentation (notarized passport-grade ID) and a video KYC interview with an authorised bank compliance officer. If the bank's risk appetite classifies the structure as High Risk because of offshore trust protectors or a Cook Islands nexus, a physical callback or an in-person interview with a director holding an existing New Zealand banking relationship may be imposed as a condition precedent to account opening. Remote opening is otherwise permitted through Accredited Third-Party KYC (AUP) under the AML/CFT Code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident corporate and trust ownership structure obscuring ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) in the International Company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extract from the New Zealand Companies Office or the Cook Islands International Registry; full organisational chart; notarised register of directors, shareholders, and UBOs; trust deed, protector letter, and registered trustee confirmation; completed AML/CFT Beneficial Ownership Declaration; sworn statement of sources of wealth and funds for each UBO; legal opinion from a New Zealand-licensed counsel confirming the entity's purpose and control matrix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-Exempt-Zone classification misinterpreted as tax evasion, a money-laundering predicate, or a shell-company indicator
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Binding tax ruling or Inland Revenue confirmation of the tax-exempt status; proof of substantive business substance including physical lease, local staffing contracts, and an ISIC 7490 project pipeline for multilingual translation and media dubbing; audited or management financial statements; client agreements and vendor contracts demonstrating genuine commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border outbound payments to numerous small counterparties typical of a localization agency supply chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transaction reconstruction file: signed master service agreements, purchase orders, itemised invoices, translator and dubbing-studio credentials, ISIC 7490 scope certificates; projected monthly disbursement schedule using Wise_B2B and Payoneer rails; documented AML risk rating classifying the industry as Low_Risk_Standard under the AML/CFT Act 2009.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection originating from heightened-risk jurisdictions or a trust-protected offshore base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds package: 12-month bank statements of the remitting entity, underlying capital contribution resolution, intercompany loan agreement if applicable, tax-residency certificates of remitters, W8-BEN-E or W9 forms, chain-of-title documents proving lawful provenance, annual statutory financial statements, and a confirmation that the funds are non-political and unencumbered.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 to the New Zealand bank account with a compliant beneficiary reference of 'CAP-CONTRIBUTION / CK_IC / NZL' or 'INTERCO-LOAN' plus a transaction purpose code aligned to ISIC 7490 services capitalisation. The remitting bank must include the International Company's legal entity identifier, the ultimate remitter's name and account number in field 50, and a detailed purpose-of-payment text in field 70 to avoid AML/CFT suspension. For equity injections, the board capital-resolution and updated shareholder register must be lodged with the New Zealand Companies Office, and the receiving bank will perform source-of-funds verification for any credit above NZD 10,000 equivalent. If the injection derives from a connected offshore trust, the trust deed, protector consent, and an NRWT exemption declaration must accompany the funds within 48 hours of receipt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for cross-border royalties, translator fees, and SaaS or media-platform settlements, with ISO 20022 payments via Payments NZ for domestic NZD legs; beneficiary bank and BIC or IBAN must be verified through a KYB check. For large-scale dubbing or co-production contracts, a Commercial Letter of Credit issued under UCP600 and advised by the vendor's bank provides irrevocable settlement security. Same-day NZD settlement occurs through the New Zealand Clearing and Settlement System operated by Payments NZ, and FX conversions are executed with the settlement bank's dealing desk to avoid double conversion. Wise_B2B and Payoneer serve as auxiliary disbursement rails for small-scale contractor payouts below NZD 5,000 where a full MT103 is economically inefficient, but the monthly aggregate routed through EMIs should not exceed 30% of total outbound trade value to preserve a clean banking profile.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards up to 12 months on NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/GBP, NZD/AUD, and NZD/CNH with an NZ Registered Bank dealing desk
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permissible only on non-deliverable emerging-market currency legs, such as NZD/IDR, NZD/PHP, and NZD/BDT, where local delivery is legally or practically impossible
Cross-currency swaps on NZD against USD, EUR, and GBP for tenor-matched hedging of intercompany loans and capital injections
Vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars on NZD pairs for protecting localization-agency contract receivables
Rolling intra-month FX spot conversions via the bank's electronic trading platform for Wise_B2B and Payoneer settlement sweeps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within the period commencing 20 working days after the company's set annual return date (not more than 12 months after the previous annual return date; typically the incorporation anniversary) and ending on the last working day of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 200 (approx USD 120) per annual return; persistent failure triggers Registrar removal (strike-off) action under Companies Act 1993 ss 318-321, with deregistration and director prohibition consequences

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (Financial Reporting Act 2013; Companies Act 1993 ss 200-209)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after balance date where the company is not exempt from financial statement preparation and filing (large companies, overseas companies, issuers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or non-GAAP filing may incur infringement fees and Registrar enforcement; continued failure supports strike-off and imposes director liability, including disqualification action

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Income Tax Return (IR4) exemption confirmation or nil return (Tax Administration Act 1994)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 7 July following the standard 31 March balance date (or within 4 months after an approved early or late balance date); the tax-exempt International Company files a nil return or written confirmation of non-resident/tax-exempt status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties (NZD 250 initial plus monthly escalation, capped) and late payment interest at the prescribed rate per Tax Administration Act 1994; unresolved amounts trigger IRD collection action, terminal tax obligations, and potential director personal liability

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if the company is 'large' (total assets exceed NZD 60 million or revenue exceeds NZD 10 million), is an FMC reporting entity (issuer), or is an overseas company required to file; the localized professional translation and media dubbing agency under the SME profile is not ordinarily large and may rely on the audit exemption unless shareholders require audit under the Companies Act 1993 or a governing shareholders' deed
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Tier 1 - NZ IFRS as issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB) for large profit-oriented entities; Tier 2 - NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR) or NZ GAAP simplified disclosure standards for non-large reporting entities; micro-businesses may apply the XRB's simple format A/S framework

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Annual Return requires the company to electronically confirm the Companies Office records of directors, shareholders, and shareholdings as at the annual return date; there is no standalone UBO public register filing yet in New Zealand, but the licensed corporate agent must complete AML/CFT Act 2009 customer due diligence on every shareholding transfer and refresh beneficial ownership data annually as ongoing monitoring; changes of directors and shareholdings must be notified to the Companies Office within 10 working days of the change

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 - 420 per annum (NZD 300 - 700) for licensed corporate agent, registered office, and annual return filing support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 25,000 (NZD 10,000 - 40,000) for a certified SME audit where triggered; no audit fee incurred where the non-large audit exemption applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (Income Tax Act 2007, Schedule 1, Part A) for New Zealand-resident companies; a non-resident company is taxed at the same 28% rate but only on New Zealand-source income and income attributable to a New Zealand branch or permanent establishment.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand does not grant general tax holidays. Targeted incentives include: (i) R&D tax credit of 15% on eligible research and development expenditure; (ii) refundable loss tax credit of 28% on R&D losses in specified circumstances; (iii) exemption for non-resident companies deriving no New Zealand-source income and not carrying on business through a New Zealand permanent establishment (the 'Tax Exempt Zone' classification asserted in this structure); (iv) no capital gains tax on most asset disposals; and (v) dividends received by a New Zealand company from a foreign company may qualify for the foreign dividend exemption subject to participation thresholds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed exclusively via the Inland Revenue (IR) secure electronic portal 'myIR' or through approved tax-return software; paper filing is disfavoured and may attract a larger compliance burden.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: A company with a standard 31 March balance date must file the IR4 by 7 July (non-tax-agent); terminal tax for the same standard balance date is payable by 7 February of the following income year. IRD-approved tax agents may receive extended filing deadlines (commonly to 28 February of the following year). Non-standard balance dates carry IRD-adjusted due dates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identity and IRD number, registered legal name, trading name, and registered office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies without a New Zealand permanent establishment are typically not obliged to file the IR4. If a New Zealand branch exists, enter the branch's New Zealand IRD number and the foreign parent's jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance date and accounting basis (standard 31 March or IRD-approved non-standard balance date; GST/HST and financial reporting basis).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the New Zealand branch balance date; a non-resident without New Zealand-source income should not file and should instead confirm nil registration status with IRD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total business income derived (New Zealand-source gross income before deductions), including localization, translation, dubbing, and media service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only New Zealand-source income is reportable. Fee income earned outside New Zealand by a non-resident from overseas clients is not assessable in New Zealand even if remitted to a New Zealand bank account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses attributable to New Zealand business income (production costs, subcontractor fees, voice-talent payments, software licences, rent, salaries).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are limited to expenses incurred in deriving assessable New Zealand-source income; general overheads of a foreign head office may be disallowed unless allocable to the New Zealand branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net assessable profit or loss before loss offsets and adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident branch must compute net profit using arm's-length transfer pricing adjustments; use of notional profit or cost-plus allocations must be supported by documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses carried forward and applied (subject to 49% shareholder continuity of beneficial ownership or, for losses incurred from 29 March 2020, the business continuity test).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the non-resident entity has a New Zealand branch and an NZ loss history, attach continuity schedules and confirm the code of ownership is maintained at each relevant time.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: imputation credits, resident withholding tax (RWT), non-resident withholding tax (NRWT), provisional tax paid, and foreign tax credits under a New Zealand DTA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branches may credit NRWT withheld on their New Zealand interest/royalty income; dividend imputation credits are not available to non-resident shareholders on branch assessments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable or refundable: taxable income taxed at 28%, after reduction for credits; shortfall assessed with use-of-money interest (UOMI) if underpaid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If all fields are nil because the company is a foreign-incorporated International Company outside the New Zealand tax net, the IR4 should not be filed; the entity should instead maintain a written non-residence position and documentary evidence of offshore management and control.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 for the first month or part-month, escalating to a maximum of NZ$1,000 for persistent non-filing; late payment penalty of 1% of unpaid tax charged on the day after the due date, a further 4% on the 7th day after the due date, and 4% each subsequent month until settled; use-of-money interest at the IRD-prescribed market rate compounds on unpaid provisional and terminal tax; criminal prosecution for failure to file a return is possible under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Provisional Tax Instalment Scheme (payment obligations administered through the IR4 assessment and myIR; no separate return form required, instalment dates are set by statute).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, payable in three instalments (for standard balance-date companies).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 March balance-date company, provisional tax instalments are due on 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May of the relevant income-year cycle; terminal tax is due 7 February following the balance date (non-tax-agent) or 7 April with an approved tax agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: First provisional payment based on estimated current-year taxable income or the previous year's standard (uplifted) liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company with no New Zealand PE has no New Zealand provisional tax obligation; a non-resident branch must estimate its New Zealand taxable income at 28% and pay instalments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Second provisional instalment, revising the estimate to reflect year-to-date results.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revisions require a revised estimate filed via myIR; underpayment exposes the branch to UOMI from the first instalment date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final provisional instalment completing the year's provisional liability before terminal tax reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branches must ensure the aggregate instalments approximate 100% of the residual income tax; safe-harbour rules allow avoidance of UOMI if the final liability is within 5% of the estimate and exceeds an IRD-set monetary threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Underpayment of provisional tax attracts UOMI calculated as if unpaid from the due date of each instalment; no separate late-filing penalty applies; deliberate underestimation may trigger the 'unacceptable tax position' shortfall penalty of 20%–40% under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR67 (Non-Resident Withholding Tax and Resident Withholding Tax Return) - withholding return filed by the New Zealand payer through myIR or approved payroll/intermediary software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Monthly (due by the 20th day of the following month); six-monthly filing permitted only for IRD-approved small payers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Monthly returns are due on the 20th of the month following payment; annual reconciliation of withholding accruals is completed in the IR4.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate dividends distributed by the New Zealand-resident company to shareholders during the month.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the shareholder is non-resident, checkbox 'Non-resident' and withheld NRWT at the statutory 30% unless a valid DTA rate declaration (IR679) and foreign tax residency certificate reduce the rate to 15% or 5%; if the shareholder is resident, withhold RWT at the elected rate (commonly 33% for individuals and 28% for resident companies).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B - Total interest paid to non-residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross interest remitted to non-residents on loans, deposits, or advances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold NRWT at 15% statutory rate; if the payer is an 'approved issuer' under section 86 of the Stamp and Cheque Duties Act 1971 and, elects approved issuer levy (AIL), no NRWT is withheld and AIL of 2% is paid; treaty declarations may reduce interest NRWT to 10% (or 0% for certain exempt government/certain financial institution interest).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C - Royalties paid to non-residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross royalties and licence fees for IP (scripts, software, dubbing masters, trademark, know-how) paid to a non-resident beneficial owner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold NRWT at the statutory 15% rate; treaty rates generally reduce royalties to 10%–15% (some treaties 5% for cultural/industrial royalties); the royalty source is New Zealand if paid by a New Zealand resident or deductible against a New Zealand PE - a foreign-to-foreign licence without New Zealand-source nexus is outside NRWT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold NRWT/RWT at source renders the payer personally liable for the full amount under section RF 9 of the Income Tax Act 2007; late filing and late payment penalties apply (NZ$250 late filing penalty, 1%+4% late payment penalty); 150% civil tax evasion penalties can apply for deliberate withholding fraud, plus imprisonment up to 5 years under section 143A.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% statutory non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends paid by a New Zealand-resident company to a non-resident shareholder (Income Tax Act 2007, s RF 7). Resident shareholders are subject to resident withholding tax (RWT) at the statutory default rate of 33% (28% election available for resident companies). Most New Zealand DTAs reduce the dividend NRWT rate to 15% for portfolio investments and 5% for corporate shareholdings of 10% or more (subject to treaty-specific limitations and beneficial-ownership clauses).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief at source, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) execute the IRD 'Non-Resident Withholding Tax Rate Declaration' (form IR679); (ii) attach the current Certificate of Residence issued by the foreign tax authority (which must certify residence in the treaty jurisdiction and beneficial ownership of the income); and (iii) lodge the declaration with the New Zealand paying company before the dividend/royalty/interest payment date. The New Zealand payer must be satisfied that the disclosure is true and correct. Where NRWT was withheld at the statutory rate, the non-resident may file a New Zealand income tax assessment (IR4 or IR3) to claim the treaty-reduced rate and obtain a refund; the refund is subject to the 4-year statutory amendment period under the Tax Administration Act 1994.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on cross-border royalties: 15% of gross royalties. Statutory NRWT on cross-border interest: 15% of gross interest; a New Zealand borrower that is an approved issuer may instead pay the 2% approved issuer levy (AIL) on interest (no NRWT). Treaty rates: dividend NRWT falls to 15% / 5% (10%+ shareholding); interest NRWT commonly 10%–15% (some treaties 0% for specified financial institutions); royalty NRWT typically 10%–15% (with some treaties providing 5% for copyright or cultural/industrial royalties, and 0% for pure 'industrial, commercial or scientific equipment' payments under older treaties). All treaty claims require the same IR679 declaration and certificate-of-residence protocol described above.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand transfer-pricing legislation is contained in sections GC 6–GC 14 of the Income Tax Act 2007 and requires all cross-border related-party dealings to be priced on an arm's-length basis. There is no legislative de minimis threshold, but IRD administrative guidance (Transfer Pricing Guidelines) states that full contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation should be maintained where aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZ$10 million; simplified documentation is expected for transactions between NZ$3 million and NZ$10 million; below NZ$3 million, the IRD still requires a reasonable written analysis of the pricing position. For this localization agency (ISIC 7490), intercompany translation services, voice-talent fees, project-management charges, and any payable or receivable balances with related parties in the Cook Islands, Asia-Pacific, or Europe must be supported by OECD-compliant benchmarking.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP) - preferred for standard translation services with published market rates
Resale Price Method - used for distribution of dub-ready media content
Cost Plus Method - dominant approach for intercompany localization service fees (cost base with arm's-length markup)
Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) - accepted for routine project-management and localization back-office services
Profit Split Method - applied where both parties contribute unique intangibles (e.g., multilingual IP libraries, dubbing catalogs, proprietary translation memory)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR); however, the IRD enforces equivalent substance requirements through: (i) the general anti-avoidance rule (Income Tax Act 2007, s BG 1) permitting the Commissioner to void arrangements whose dominant purpose is tax avoidance; (ii) the company-residence rule (s YD 2) under which a foreign-incorporated company becomes a New Zealand tax resident if its head office is in New Zealand or its directors exercise central management and control in New Zealand; and (iii) the thin capitalisation rules (s FE) restricting debt deductions of multinational groups. For the 'Tax Exempt Zone' classification of the CK_IC International Company to hold, the entity must maintain offshore board meetings, offshore decision-making, a substantive physical presence outside New Zealand, and derive no income sourced in New Zealand. A bare shell with New Zealand-resident directors, local project management, or New Zealand bank/fintech accounts (Wise B2B, Payoneer) collecting global localization revenue is presumptively at risk of being re-characterised as a New Zealand-resident taxpayer or as an abusive tax arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating New Zealand-source income (e.g., routing fees for translation and dubbing contracts performed in New Zealand through a non-resident shell, omitting branch profits from the IR4, or fabricating invoices to shift profits to the offshore International Company).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil shortfall penalty of 150% of the evaded tax for evasion or a related offence, 100% for an 'abusive tax position', 40% for gross carelessness, and 20%–40% for an unacceptable tax position (Tax Administration Act 1994, s 141); criminal conviction under s 143A attracts a fine up to NZ$250,000 (body corporate) or NZ$50,000 (individual) and/or imprisonment up to 5 years; falsifying records under s 143B carries an additional 5-year imprisonment exposure; the Commissioner can issue a departure prohibition order under s 157 preventing directors from leaving New Zealand while tax debts are outstanding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the company is used as a sham or where directors 'direct, authorise, acquiesce in, or participate in' tax evasion: directors and shadow controllers are jointly and severally liable for the company's tax shortfall; personal prosecution with imprisonment up to 5 years is available; a civil liability notice may be issued against directors for unpaid withholding tax (PAYE/GST) under the director penalty provisions; travel bans under s 157 apply to individuals with outstanding tax liabilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the CK_IC International Company as a tax-exempt vehicle while all economic activity (project negotiation, translation production, dubbing recording, media localization, and revenue generation) is factually conducted in New Zealand by New Zealand-resident personnel; failure to hold genuine offshore board meetings; presence of New Zealand-resident directors with no independent offshore oversight.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IRD will disregard the offshore entity under GAAR (s BG 1) and assess the economic income as derived by the New Zealand PE or by the underlying New Zealand actors; 100% abusive-tax-position shortfall penalty; 150% if evasion is shown; the arrangement is void against the Commissioner; criminal prosecution for false declarations under s 143B; the foreign company is also exposed to Companies Office deregistration for non-compliance with the Companies Act 1993.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who permit the company to be used as a sham may be personally assessed as a result of the 'clean-skin' test under the Companies Act 1993 (permitting the court to grant leave to pierce the veil where the company is carrying on a sham); directors face civil liability for losses caused; prosecution for fraud (Crimes Act 1961 s 240-241) with imprisonment up to 7 years; departure prohibition orders may be imposed for assessed tax.
